sections.heading: 1. Car seat set-up
lines: ① Distance: pedals down, knees slightly bent.
② Backrest: a slight recline, lumbar support set.
③ Wheel: back on seat, wrists reach the top.
④ On long drives, take a break every 2 hours.

caption:
Mr Turtle drives 90 minutes a day, and when he gets out of the car his back takes a while to straighten.

Driving means sitting in one position for a long time, so your seat set-up matters.

Hybi's three steps: sit close enough that your knees stay slightly bent with the pedals fully down, recline the backrest slightly and set the lumbar support, and check your wrists reach the top of the wheel with your back on the seat. On long drives, take a break every two hours.

Pain spreading down a leg, tingling, or no change after two weeks are worth an assessment. Our chiropractors at Hybrid Physio can help. Book online via the link in bio 🚗
